il-lake-2026-treasurer-hart-sandy.name: Sandy Hart
il-lake-2026-treasurer-hart-sandy.bio: Lake County Board Chair and longtime District 13 board member, first elected to the board in 2012.

positions.stance: Will ensure internal and external controls on every County investment, applying "safety of principal first, prudent diversity of funds, and proper liquidity."
Will keep investments, payments, and financial records easily accessible to the public and deliver accurate, timely property tax distributions to every taxing body.
Pledges to "listen to understand, debate respectfully, and seek common ground," saying "government works best when you don't know it's there."

il-lake-2026-sheriff-buchberger-roman.name: Roman Buchberger
il-lake-2026-sheriff-buchberger-roman.bio: Army veteran and career law enforcement officer who has worked in patrol, investigations, training, and as a supervisor.

positions.stance: Will restore full patrol staffing in unincorporated Lake County, increase visibility, and invest in proactive strategies to prevent crime.
Will launch a 90-day staffing recovery plan, promote based on performance rather than favoritism, and "work in good faith with the union."
Will end the county's dependency on housing inmates in McHenry County by recruiting officers, and will expand jail rehabilitation programs.
Will expand school outreach programs bringing deputies into schools for mentorship and partner with the College of Lake County on jail job training.

il-lake-2026-sheriff-idleburg-john.name: John D. Idleburg
il-lake-2026-sheriff-idleburg-john.bio: Lake County Sheriff; Marine Corps veteran and retired U.S. Treasury Department special agent.

positions.stance: Has "dedicated resources to aggressively pursue trafficking in all its forms (guns, human, drugs) to keep our community safe."
Says his office implemented a duty-to-intervene policy on excessive force before the SAFE-T Act legally required it.
"Sheriff has and will always, in good faith, work with unions to resolve challenges collaboratively and ensure their collective bargaining rights are respected."

il-will-2026-clerk-parker-annette.name: Annette Parker
il-will-2026-clerk-parker-annette.bio: Will County Clerk since 2024; former Will County Board member, President of the Forest Preserve District of Will County, and Lockport Chamber of Commerce executive director.

il-will-2026-sheriff-reilly-james.name: James "Jim" Reilly
il-will-2026-sheriff-reilly-james.bio: Will County Sheriff's deputy since 2013; previously spent eight years with the Joliet Police Department.

positions.stance: Will strengthen the connection between law enforcement and neighborhoods to foster trust and ensure responsiveness to community needs.
Will implement modern ethical-policing practices so the office's actions are "open to public scrutiny."
Will continue to support the men and women in law enforcement so residents feel safe and secure in their community.
Will expand partnerships with treatment and crisis centers to address "the root causes of crime."
Supports school safety programs and youth outreach initiatives to create a secure environment for students.

il-will-2026-sheriff-jones-patrick.name: Patrick Jones
il-will-2026-sheriff-jones-patrick.bio: Will County Sheriff's Office sergeant who joined the office in 2001; SWAT operator and crisis negotiator.

positions.stance: Says improving the partnership between the Sheriff's Office and the community is essential for building trust and protecting residents.
Promises "clear communication, consistent collaboration with other local leaders," and encouraging community involvement in the Sheriff's Office.
Intends to provide tools at the Will County Adult Detention Facility to prepare individuals for a productive life after release.

il-will-2026-treasurer-maurella-carmen.name: Carmen Maurella III
il-will-2026-treasurer-maurella-carmen.bio: Homer Township Assessor, accounting educator at Lewis University and College of DuPage, and accounting and tax business owner.

il-will-2026-treasurer-brophy-tim.name: Tim Brophy
il-will-2026-treasurer-brophy-tim.bio: Will County Treasurer since 2018; banking and real estate lending professional and former four-term Joliet City Councilman.

ga-cobb-2026-solicitor-metzger-makia.name: Makia Metzger
ga-cobb-2026-solicitor-metzger-makia.bio: Cobb County Solicitor General since her 2022 election, with an 18-year prosecutorial career in two metro Atlanta counties.

positions.stance: Says "mass incarceration is not only expensive on taxpayers, but a gateway to wayward low-level offenders becoming more violent criminals."
Says she has created "second chances when appropriate" and ensured cases are prosecuted "with compassion, grace and efficiency."
Redirecting resources to target the greatest threats, support crime victims immediately, and reduce low-level reoffending through restorative accountability.
Believes "justice should be fair, firm and restorative"; has no blanket filing policies and expanded the diversion program for low-level offenders.
Requires nationally credentialed victim advocates, Marsy's Law compliance, and created a Special Victims Unit for complex crimes.
Will continue prevention-education programs addressing domestic abuse, senior protection, teen safety, and drunk driving.
Will work with law enforcement, policy makers, and community stakeholders on reforms that reduce crime and create healthier outcomes.

nc-durham-2026-sheriff-birkhead-clarence.name: Clarence F. Birkhead
nc-durham-2026-sheriff-birkhead-clarence.bio: Durham County Sheriff since 2018; former Chief of Police in Hillsborough and at Duke University Public Safety.

positions.stance: Says he is "actively engaged in the fight for criminal justice reform" and serves on the Governor's Task Force for Racial Equity in Criminal Justice.
Has rejected ICE detainers without a judicial warrant or a Notice to Appear, saying "detainers target marginalized communities."
Banned "no-knock warrants" by policy.
Implemented all aspects of "8 Can't Wait" use-of-force policies.
Increased efforts to remove drugs and guns from communities, including a regional strike team across four counties targeting violent offenders.

nc-durham-2026-district-attorney-deberry.name: Satana Deberry
nc-durham-2026-district-attorney-deberry.bio: Durham District Attorney for two terms; former General Counsel for the NC Department of Health and Human Services and executive director of the NC Housing Coalition.

mi-macomb-2026-county-executive-hackel-m.name: Mark A. Hackel
mi-macomb-2026-county-executive-hackel-m.bio: Macomb County Executive, the county's first; former Macomb County Sheriff.

positions.stance: Cites eliminating a $52 million budget gap, balancing all county budgets, and raising the county's bond ratings.
Mark "firmly believes that the public provides an important role in providing oversight to government" and should see how resources are used.
Established the Macomb County Ethics Board to provide independent oversight of county government.

mi-macomb-2026-county-executive-moore-ri.name: Richard Moore
mi-macomb-2026-county-executive-moore-ri.bio: Army veteran and controls design engineer at JR Automation.

positions.stance: Will work to attract new businesses to Macomb County by creating a favorable environment for investment and innovation.
Will partner closely with law enforcement, providing resources and support to make Macomb County "the safest in the state."
Will invest in sustainable solutions, efficient repairs, and planning for future transportation needs to make county roads "the best in the state."

nj-bergen-2026-county-executive-hennesse.name: Todd H. Hennessey
nj-bergen-2026-county-executive-hennesse.bio: Retired from the Port Authority of New York & New Jersey; former chairman of Transit Workers Union Local 2001 and small business owner.

positions.stance: Wants to stop overdevelopment in small towns and opposes tax abatements for wealthy developers, unnecessary bonding, wasteful spending, and patronage jobs.
Would lower electric bills by upgrading grid infrastructure, reopen closed power plants, and petition the utility authority on gas costs.
Proposes paid apprenticeships and internships inside county government, partnered with local employers, trade unions, technical schools, and Bergen Community College.
Will work with the Superintendent of Elections to remove deceased and non-Bergen County residents from voter registration rolls.
Would protect and expand veterans' housing and health outreach and adjust property taxes seniors cannot afford.

nj-bergen-2026-county-executive-tedesco-.name: James J. Tedesco III
nj-bergen-2026-county-executive-tedesco-.bio: Bergen County Executive and 50-year volunteer firefighter.

positions.stance: Cites "keeping Bergen County among the safest places to live."
Cites eliminating chronic and veteran homelessness in Bergen County.
Investing in infrastructure by paving roads, rebuilding bridges, installing broadband, and upgrading County parks.
Supporting education by restoring funding cut by the previous administration and increasing the allocation twelve years in a row.
Cites "maintaining one of the lowest tax rates in New Jersey."
